questions.question: Pandit Birju Maharaj was conferred with which of the following awards?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Padma Vibhushan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Birju Maharaj **was conferred with **the Padma Vibhushan award**.
 
• Padma Vibhushan is the second-highest civilian award in India, which is given for exceptional and distinguished service in any field including service rendered by government servants.
 
• Shaurya Chakra is a military award given for acts of gallantry in the face of the enemy.
 
• Padma Bhushan is the third-highest civilian award in India, which is given for distinguished service of a high order in any field, including service rendered by government servants.
 
• Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award in India, which is given for distinguished service in any field.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Indian dancer, singer, composer, and representative of the **Lucknow "Kalka-Bindadin" Gharana of Kathak dance** was **Pandit Birju Maharaj**.
 
• His father and guru, Acchan Maharaj, as well as his two uncles, Shambhu Maharaj and Lachhu Maharaj, were all members of the Maharaj family of Kathak dancers.
 
• He began his career with his uncle Shambhu Maharaj, working alongside him at Bhartiya Kala Kendra and then Kathak Kendra in New Delhi.
 
• He led the latter organization for a number of years before retiring in 1998 to start his own dance school, Kalashram, in Delhi.

questions.question: Who among the following was a saint from Maharashtra?
Padma Shri awardee, Gaddam Padmaja Reddy was associated with which classical dance of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuchipudi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **President Kovind** presents Padma Shri to **Gaddam Padmaja Reddy **for **Art. An internationally renowned Kuchipudi dancer**, she has **been performing for over fifty years **now.
 
• She has **worked relentlessly **to **promote Kuchipudi**.
 
• **Kuchipudi **is **a dance-drama performance**, with **its roots in the ancient Hindu Sanskrit text **of **Natya Shastra**. It developed as a **religious art **linked to **traveling bards**, **temples**, and **spiritual beliefs**, like **all major classical dances **of **India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Manipuri Dance **also referred to as **the Manipuri Raas Leela**, is **one of the eight major Indian classical dance forms**, originating from the **state of Manipur**.
 
• **Sattriya**, or **Sattriya Nritya**, is a **major Indian classical dance**. It is a **dance-drama performance art **with **origins in the Krishna-centered Vaishnavism monasteries **of **Assam **and **attributed to the 15th-century Bhakti movement **scholar and **saint Mahapurush Srimanta Sankardev.**
 
• **Kathak is one of the eight major **forms of **Indian classical dance**. It is the **classical dance **form of **Uttar Pradesh**. The **origin of Kathak **is **traditionally attributed **to **the traveling bards **of **ancient northern India **known as **Kathakars or storytellers**.

questions.question: The ‘Servants of India Society’ was founded by which of the following freedom fighters?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gopal Krishna Gokhale**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Servants of India Society was founded by **Gopal Krishna Gokhale** on **June 12, 1905** in Pune, Maharashtra.
 
• The primary aim of the society was to train individuals for public service and to promote social and political reforms in India.
 
• Gokhale envisioned the society as a group of selfless workers who would dedicate their lives to the betterment of the country and its people.
 
• The society emphasized education, healthcare, and the upliftment of the underprivileged as core areas of focus.
 
• It played a significant role in fostering the spirit of nationalism and preparing young Indians to contribute to the Indian freedom movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gopal Krishna Gokhale:**

 
 
• He was a senior leader of the Indian National Congress and a mentor to Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• He advocated for moderate reforms and emphasized constitutional methods for achieving self-rule.
 
 
 
• **Servants of India Society Objectives:**
 
 
• Promotion of education, especially among marginalized sections of society.
 
• Upliftment of the poor and eradication of social evils like untouchability and caste discrimination.
 
 
 
• **Prominent Members:**
 
 
• Key members of the society included Srinivasa Shastri and Dattatraya Balkrishna Kalelkar, who furthered its goals.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• The society's work laid the groundwork for broader social and political reforms in India, influencing future leaders of the independence movement.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first Biologist who discovered cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Robert Hooke.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Robert Hooke** discovered** cells in 1665** while examining a thin slice of **cork under a microscope.**
 
• **Rosalind Franklin **was a** chemist and X-ray crystallographer** who made significant contributions to the discovery of the** structure of DNA.**
 
• **Gregor Mendel **was an **Augustinian friar and scientist** who is known as the father of modern genetics for his pioneering work in **pea plant breeding.**
 
• **Charles Darwin** was a **naturalist and biologist** who is best known for his** theory of evolution** by natural selection.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cells **are the **basic structural and functional units **of living organisms, and the discovery of cells marked a major milestone in the development of modern biology.
 
• Robert Hooke's **discovery of cells **was made possible by the** invention of the microscope**, which allowed scientists to see structures that were too small to be seen with the naked eye.
 
• **Rosalind Franklin's **work on X-ray crystallography was instrumental in the discovery of the **double helix structure of DNA,** but she died before the **Nobel Prize** was awarded to her colleagues James Watson, Francis Crick, and Maurice Wilkins in 1962.
 
• **Gregor Mendel's experiments** with pea plants laid the foundation for the **modern science of genetics, **but his work was largely ignored by the scientific community until the early 20th century.
 
• **Charles Darwin's theory of evolution** by natural selection revolutionized our understanding of the** diversity of life on Earth, **but it was based on observations of living organisms rather than the structure of cells.
